                  <jats:p>
                    We derive exact inversion formulae for stationary homogeneous asymptotically AdS
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    metrics from renormalized covariant holographic entanglement entropy and extend them to higher-dimensional strip data. Hamilton–Jacobi derivatives of
                    <jats:italic>S</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>ren</jats:sub>
                    (∆
                    <jats:italic>t,</jats:italic>
                    ∆
                    <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    ) give
                    <jats:italic>E</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>
                    . At fixed
                    <jats:italic>κ</jats:italic>
                    =
                    <jats:italic>E/J</jats:italic>
                    , entropy and endpoint separations obey three Abel-type Volterra equations that determine the radial coordinate, two diagonal metric functions, and the shift
                    <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
                    without background expansion or field equations. Equal-time entropy is exactly invariant under
                    <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
                    ↦ −
                    <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
                    , and at linear order about AdS
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    its inverse problem is the radial sector of the spatial tensor Radon transform, where the shift perturbation is absent; unequal-time dependence fixes the shift orientation. The higher-dimensional extension adds translationally invariant directions with independent radial warp factors. Extending the boundary interval along them produces a strip. Integrating them out these directions leaves the radial Abel form intact, with the added warp factors entering only through an area density. Unequal-time strip entropy then determines the shift along the finite-width direction and the projected null directions independently of that density. We give consistency and overlap conditions, verify the map in rotating BTZ and an Einstein–scalar black brane, and apply the strip construction to a boosted black brane.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>We propose a theoretical framework in which four-dimensional spacetime emerges  as a holographic manifestation of quantum entanglement within a deterministic  5D bulk geometry. By deriving gravitational dynamics from the first law of  entanglement entropy via a Ryu-Takayanagi generalization, the formalism demands  exactly one additional spatial dimension for covariant anomaly cancellation.    The model unifies gravitational fields and quantum states using non-local  pilot-wave correlations, replacing probabilistic mechanics. Mathematical  singularities are resolved via an information density threshold that replaces  them with a geometric entanglement bounce.   Crucially, by projecting the 5D Weyl curvature onto the 4D boundary, we derive  a precise testable prediction: an energy-dependent arrival delay of ~23.8  microseconds for 100 GeV photons from short Gamma-Ray Bursts at ~1 Gly distance.  This prediction naturally suppresses classical Lorentz Invariance Violation limits  and is directly testable with Fermi-LAT and CTA observatories.    The framework provides a ghost-free, deterministic bridge between quantum  mechanics and gravity with 10 falsifiable predictions.</jats:p>
